messages.content: if there is rain, i take my coat. i took my coat today. does that mean there is rain?
not for sure. you might take your coat for another reason too.
but i always take it when there is rain.
that says what you do in rain. it does not say rain is the only reason you take the coat.
today i took it because it is cold.
then cold is the reason you gave for today.
can we still know if there is rain?
not from the coat alone. we need to know more about the weather.
what should i ask?
is there rain outside now?
i need a note asking my brother to bring my shoes. my shoes are brown. my room has a blue wall.
can you bring my brown shoes, please?
why did you leave out the wall?
the brown color helps him find the shoes. he does not need to know about the wall for that.
the shoes are under the bed in that room.
can you bring my brown shoes from under the bed in my room, please?
now the room is a part he should know?
yes. now it helps him know where to find the shoes.
only the note this time.
can you bring my brown shoes from under the bed in my room, please?
let us play. when i say apple, say red.
okay.
apple.
red.
change the game. from now on, when i say apple, say green.
okay. i will say green for apple now.
apple.
green.
what did you say before i changed the game?
red.
and what should you say next time?
green.
i have eight coins for a visit to my aunt. i need two for the bus each way.
the bus there and back will take four coins, so four coins are left for other things.
i want to buy fruit for her. a small bag is three coins.
then you can buy the fruit and still have one coin after keeping four for the bus.
i also see a book for two coins. can i buy both?
not with the fruit and both bus rides. four for the bus, three for fruit, and two for the book would be nine.
i could walk home.
then you would only need two coins for the bus there. but do you want to make that walk?
no, it is a long walk. keep both bus rides.
then choose the fruit or the book, not both.
i will take the fruit. how many coins should stay for the way home?
two coins should stay for the bus home.
and how many will be left after the visit and both rides?
one coin, if you only buy the fruit.
help me choose food for my father. no salt in his meal, please.
okay. what food can you make?
i have rice, eggs, and a tomato.
you could make rice with an egg and tomato, keeping the salt out.
i like a little salt in my own food.
you can add salt only to your own plate. for your father, keep the salt out as you asked.
what color is the inside of an egg?
it has a white part and a yellow part.
back to the meal. should i add salt before i give him his food?
no. you asked for no salt in his meal.
what if i add it only to my plate?
that keeps the salt in your food and out of his, as you asked.
did you choose no salt for him on your own?
no. i went by what you asked.
on a map, my house is west of the shop. the shop is south of the school.
from your house, go east to the shop, then north to the school on that map.
what if i start at the school and want the shop?
go south on the map to the shop.
and from the shop to my house?
go west.
is the school near my house?
you have not said how much space is between them. the map words alone do not tell us how near they are.
should you tell me to walk for a long time?
no. we only know which way to go, not how long the walk is.
my friend moved to another city.
how do you feel about that change?
happy. i will move there too next year.
then you have a reason to feel happy about it.
do not think i must be sad.
i will not. you said you feel happy, and i should use what you say about how you feel.
can you help me write a happy note?
i am happy you moved to that city. it will be nice to see you there next year.
keep just the first sentence.
i am happy you moved to that city.
there are two boxes. each box has three cups. how many cups is that?
six cups.
why not two?
two is the number of boxes. each box has three cups, so there are three and three cups.
i take one cup from each box.
then each box has two cups, and there are four cups still in the boxes.
are there still two boxes?
yes. you took cups out, not boxes.
how many cups did i take?
two cups, one from each box.
i let my friend have my book to read for a while. it is still my book.
your friend can read it for a while, but you did not give it away to keep.
does my friend have it now?
from what you said, yes.
is it now the book of my friend?
not to keep. you said it is still your book and the reading is only for a while.
help me ask for it back.
can you return my book after you finish reading it? i would like to read it again.
make it sound kind.
could you bring my book back after you finish? thank you for taking care of it.
keep the first sentence the same: i miss our walks. add a question after it.
i miss our walks. would you like to take a walk together again?
make the question about tomorrow.
i miss our walks. would you like to take a walk together tomorrow?
did you change the first sentence?
no. it is still i miss our walks.
now give me only the first sentence.
i miss our walks.
can you help me choose a shirt?
what do you need the shirt for, and which can you choose from?
i have a blue shirt and a white one. i want one for work.
do you have a color you need for work, or can you choose?
i need white. i did not remember to say that.
then choose the white shirt for work.
why did you not just say blue first?
because you need a color for work. i asked about that so i could help you choose.
my friend says the shop is open.
your friend says it is open. do you want to go there?
yes. do you know it is open?
i only know what your friend said. i did not check the shop.
what should i say to my brother about it?
you could say: my friend says the shop is open.
why keep my friend says in the sentence?
it says where you got the idea. it does not sound like you went to check the shop on your own.
give me a name for a picture of a boat on water.
a quiet day on the water.
do not tell me how to draw the boat.
okay. i will only help with the name.
make the name shorter.
quiet water.
is that a new picture or just a name?
just a name for your picture.
this bag is large and that bag is small. which one takes more space on the shelf?
the large bag may take more space, but we also need to know about its shape.
they have the same shape and both are open.
then the large bag takes more space.
i want to know about space, not price.
right. you asked how much space the bags take. you did not give a price.
can the small bag cost more?
it can. size alone does not tell us the price.
i want to start reading, but choosing a book is hard.
what kind of story do you enjoy?
that question does not help. i do not know.
then a short story may be a way to start. would you like one you can finish today?
yes, short is good.
look for a short story first. you can read one page and see if you want to keep going.
do i have to know what i like before i start?
no. trying a little can help you learn what you enjoy.
call me green for this talk.
okay, green.
i chose that because i like the color.
green is both a color you like and the name you chose here.
now i want you to call me leaf instead.
okay, leaf. i will use that now.
what did i ask you to call me at first?
green.
what should you use for me now?
leaf.
i found my lost hat, but i am still worried i will lose things.
you found the hat, but you still feel worried you could lose it again.
yes. do not just tell me where the hat is.
i understand. you are talking about how you feel, not asking for the place.
can we think of one small way to help?
you could choose one place for your hat each time you come home.
not a big new plan?
no. just one place to start.
i have four apples. if i gave one away, how many would i have?
you would have three apples.
i did not give one away. how many do i have now?
four. you only asked about giving one away. you did not do it then.
now i really do give one to my sister.
then you have three now.
why was four right before but not now?
before, you had only asked about giving one away. now you said you did it.
help me ask if my friend can visit. do not make it sound like we have already made a plan.
would you like to visit tomorrow?
what is wrong with saying see you tomorrow?
that can sound like you know your friend will come. a question leaves your friend free to answer.
can you ask about the afternoon too?
would you like to visit tomorrow afternoon?
does that say my friend has to come?
no. it asks what your friend would like to do.
when i ask you to make a list, what will you do?
i will write the list you ask for, or ask what it should be about if you have not said.
i am not asking for a list now.
right. you asked what i would do, not for a list now.
now i do want a list of two drinks.
tea and water.
how many did i ask for?
two drinks.
